### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6ff3eee7ca595cf1bb5c47e9fc09bb127c0a57d0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · PR #33707 (#33597 round 2) · 2026-11-15T07:11Z

Head-sha: `7702fe4044d18825ecbd2d0ead7565de76cc1c4e` · report 6890641277 · claim 6887965873, amendment 6889999778 · seat record 6889635350 · owner's ruling eval#1 (role strings; 2026-11-15 05:52Z) · HOLD lifted by eval#1's replay Notify 6890573292

- **Form:** draft → `main`. The body opens with the attribution block, then the `Clause-②` / `Metadata-protocol` lines and `Fixes #33597`. Round 1 (#33630, Part-of) is merged, so this round closes the card. 10 files, all inside the amended surface: the `run.personas[].role` strings of 7 cards, two tests and one changeset. No other card field, no `src/**`, no schema, no prompt code.
- **Scope (seat ruling at ~06:00Z):** a write need is untraced only when the card's FULL rendered build prompt never states it for that persona, not just its role. The thread re-derived 40 write needs over the 9 cards. The prose states 21; 19 were stated nowhere. Those 19 are now carried by 13 personas' roles in 7 cards: the 11 the seat listed, plus `client_viewer`'s refused task update and six starter-card needs, each named with its reason in the PR body. The two starter cards with no change (`order_to_cash`, `requisition_to_receipt`) keep their prompts.
- **Diff read (seat):** every role keeps its old text and appends the object and the verb. A refused write carries a negation, e.g. "Warehouse staff who may read invoices but not change them", as the owner asked. No title, provenance or other prose changes.
- **The pin (`scenario-cards.test.ts` §3 TRACE):** every write need of the library maps either to ROLE or to verbatim prose quotes in the rendered `buildPrompt`. ROLE is judged by a stated word rule: the object name, a verb word for that verb, and a negation for a refused need. The rule's limits are written next to it. A need with no entry, a reworded quote, or a reverted role turns it red; the thread ran ablations on all three. This makes done-when 2 hold for every future card.
- **Replay:** `role` also enters the run prompt ("You act for …"). The eval-r1 recording fixture is keyed by card, mode, half, operation and persona, not prompt text, so it needed no re-pin. eval#1 recorded its M1 replay on the old prompts first (6890573292) and runs live confirmation runs on these prompts next.
- **Gates:** check-runs at this head: 51 — 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 other (read this act; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success`); `mergeable_state` clean. Local (thread): package 763/763, typecheck 0, lint 0, derived gates 61/61 exit 0.
- **Contract review:** no face. There is no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, and `Clause-②: no` (only card data the package ships in `dist/library` changes; no export or type changes).
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/scenarios` patch, because the cards ship in `dist/library` and `packed-tarball.test.ts` pins them. It names the 13 personas and the run-prompt effect, which matches the diff.
- **Accepted deviations:** none.
- **Landing:** K = 0 (`git rev-list --count --first-parent 6ff3eee7..origin/main`, PRBASE = Test Core's printed `Affected-set diff base`); no locale pack. Landed on the maintainer's standing word 「按 pm-dispatch 审过的pr你可以自主落地」 (2026-10-30 14:20Z, spec seat 2 thread): `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` in this stroke.
